about: Points marked by hand: read by eye off crops of the original input, each a crop of the stated box (left, top, right, bottom, in the original's pixels) enlarged `zoom` times with a grid every `gridPx` pixels labelled in the original's pixels, the labels in a strip outside the crop. Pixel coordinates are the original's, with (0, 0) the centre of the top left pixel. I1-back is read flipped left to right (its x is 2375 less the file's). Nothing here is moved after a fit; spike.py records what it does to each mark.

scale.what: On I1-front. Rows across: the first and last pin of both rows of the ten ICs and of the expansion header P2, each the middle of the pad as read by eye, then moved to its blob's centroid by common.refine_to_pad (refused beyond 0.6 mm). Pin 1 is at the lower left of each DIP: every DIP lies with its notch to the left. Drills: pin 1 and pin N, directly across from it on the other row, of each IC, the middle of the hole as read by eye, then fitted on the hole's top rim by spike.py.

fingers.note: The end fingers of the component side, a point in the middle of each read by eye. Not refined with common.refine_to_pad, which finds round pads; spike.py puts each between its two edges (finger_centre).

outline.what: On I1-front: the outline's shape, for board_frame.py to measure. The corners in order round the board, clockwise as the scan lies, from the top left; edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1, and the last back to the first. Each corner is read by eye on its crop to about half a millimetre: it says where to look and where the outline turns, and where each edge lies is measured by board_frame.py on the light, never taken from here. The coordinates were first placed from an automatic trace of the outline by an earlier version of board_frame.py, then each was checked on its crop and moved where it was wrong: corners 0 and 1 down to the routed edge under the break-off tabs' remains (the bottoms of the half holes between them), corners 6 and 7 up to the step's edge from the shadow below it. The round notches are marked by their deepest points and the edge they are in. Edge 0, the short top left stretch, carries the remains of break-off tabs over most of its length, standing about 0.9 mm out, with half holes between them reaching down to the routed edge (the top right stretch has them over its right end only, and its straight part is most of it).

corners.what: top left: the left edge and the routed top edge of the short top left stretch, under its tabs' remains
the short top left stretch's right end, at its routed edge
the step down in the top edge, inside corner
the step back up in the top edge, inside corner
the top right stretch's left end
the right edge's step, outer corner (marked at the dark lower edge of the bare laminate, above the shadow)
the right edge's step, inside corner (as corner 6)
the right slot's right wall at the bottom edge
the right slot's top right inside corner
the right slot's top left inside corner
the right slot's left wall at the bottom edge
the left slot's right wall at the bottom edge
the left slot's top right inside corner
the left slot's top left inside corner
the left slot's left wall at the bottom edge

notches.what: the round notch in the left edge, its deepest point
the small round notch in the right edge, above the step, its deepest point
the small round notch in the right edge, just above the step, its deepest point

solderSeeds.what: Four holes far apart, each the middle of the hole read by eye on I1-front and on I1-back flipped left to right.

palLayout.what: The pins' feet where they meet the board on I3, the PAL NES-CPU-11 (the solder joint or pad of each end pin, not the leg's shoulder: a 20 mm lens leans what is tall), read by eye off crops enlarged twice with a 10 px grid; the same pins on I1-front from its pads, moved by common.refine_to_pad. Pin 1 is at the lower left of each DIP on both boards.
palLayout.crops: I3: for each IC, its four corners, each a crop of 180 by 140 px centred on the pin's place predicted from U6 and U5, enlarged twice with a 10 px grid. I1-front: the scale's tiles, and for the 300 mil rows of U1 and U4, 40 px tiles enlarged eight times with a 5 px grid.

parts.note: Both boards carry two footprints here, 600 and 300 mil, sharing the row of pins 1 to 12; I3's RAM is in the 300 mil one, so its pins 13 and 24 are marked in the 300 mil row on both boards.
Both boards carry two footprints here, 600 and 300 mil, sharing the row of pins 1 to 12; I3's RAM is in the 300 mil one, so its pins 13 and 24 are marked in the 300 mil row on both boards.
Pin 16 is under a capacitor on I3, so U3 is marked by pins 1, 8 and 9 on both boards.

notMeasured.why: On I3 the 72-pin cartridge connector is fitted over the edge fingers, so no finger can be seen.
On I3 the expansion port's socket is fitted; its body hides every pin.
On I3 the PAL modulator's can covers the place of the 5-pin MOD RF footprint that I1 shows; its own pins on its small board above the can are not the board's.

case.what: Each of the case top's four edges marked by hand as a segment along it (two points read by eye off crops enlarged two or three times with a 10 px grid, away from the rounded corners); spike.py fits a line to the edge near each segment and puts each corner where two lines meet. nearLong is the long top edge nearer the camera (the front in O2-FL, the rear in O2-BR), farLong the other, nearShort and farShort the short ones. base is a segment along the bottom edge of the near long face, where the case meets the table. An optional third number is the half width of the search across the segment, in px. verticals are two segments along the corners' vertical edges at the near long face's two ends, between the top and where the bottom shell starts: a check on the camera, not used in the figures.
case.notes: The corners' vertical edges stop where the bottom shell starts: below it the bottom shell's sides lean in, so no corner edge reaches the table. The height is read instead from the bottom edge of the near long face, through the vertical plane of that face (spike.py, case_photo). On O2-BR the near long face's bottom edge is used right of its middle notch only: left of it the edge is broken by the connector panel and the notch.

palFront.what: Lines on the front band of the top shell, each a segment marked by hand along it; spike.py fits each line. O2-FL: the band's ends are the corners' vertical edges, its top the case top's near long edge (from "case"), its bottom where the bottom shell starts, either side of the black strip; the door's left side is the middle of the dark gap beside it, its right side the black strip's left edge; POWER's left edge and RESET's right edge on the bottom shell. O4: the PAL top shell, taken apart, straight on: its band's four edges, the door's left gap and the black block's left edge.

notMeasured.why: O4 is the PAL top shell taken off its console; POWER and RESET are on the bottom shell, which O4 does not show. Measured on O2-FL and the patent, recorded.

patent.what: O1, the design patent: each view a box marked by hand round its drawing, on the PDF page pdfimages takes it from (page 3 is sheet 2, page 4 sheet 3, 2320 by 3408 px at 300 dpi), read off the sheets shrunk three times and checked on crops at full scale. front: lines on FIG 3, the front view, each a place marked by hand on a crop enlarged four times with a 5 px grid, and the run along it that is read: the top shell's two sides, its top and the seam below it (two drawn lines, read together), the door's left side (two lines) and the black strip's left edge (two lines), POWER's left and RESET's right edges (each the middle of the three lines drawn round each button).

footprints.what: On I1-front: each footprint's reference, read by eye off its crop of the print (nothing in the tools reads text): a point inside the footprint (`at`), and where the grouping cannot tell, the pairing of its rows (`rowSpacingMm`, `alternate` for a second footprint sharing a row) or its pin 1 (`pin1`, a point on the pad). A mark with `pins` groups a footprint by hand, pin by pin, each a point on its pad. board_register.py records what each mark did (registration.json "marks").

marks.reason: The print reads 'U6' and 'CPU' above the footprint's upper row at its left, and 'CPU' inside its outline.
The print reads 'U5' and 'PPU' below the footprint's lower row, and 'PPU' inside its outline.

The print reads 'U2' and '74LS373' below the footprint's lower row, and '74LS373' inside its outline. Pin 1 by hand: the print's notch is at the outline's left end, but a via sits in it and another beside it, and the print is not looked for within 1 mm of a hole, so the grouping cannot see enough of it; pin 1 is at the lower left, task 0's mark.
The print reads 'U3' and '74LS139' below the footprint's lower row, and '74LS139' inside its outline.

The print reads 'U7' and '40H368(CI)' above the footprint's upper row, and '40H368(CI)' inside its outline. Pin 1 by hand: a via sits in the outline's notch at its left end, so the grouping cannot see the notch; pin 1 is at the lower left, task 0's mark.
The print reads 'U8' and '40H368(CII)' below the footprint's lower row, and '40H368(CII)' inside its outline.
The print reads 'U10' and 'CIC' above the footprint's upper row, and 'CIC' inside its outline.
The print reads 'U9' and '74HCU04P' below the footprint's lower row, and '74HCU04P' inside its outline (the KiCad redrawing has a 74LS04 here; the scan wins, as the plan's Facts say).

The print reads 'U1' and 'SRAM(WRAM)' below the footprint's lower row. Three rows of 12 holes: the 600 mil footprint is the upper and the lower row (the plan's Facts: U1, the 6116, is a DIP-24 at 600 mil; task 0's scale marks take these two rows), drawn as a dashed outline above a solid one; the middle row and the lower are a 300 mil footprint for a narrower RAM (the PAL board's sit there, task 0). The grouping could pair the lower row either way, so the pairing is said here. The 600 mil outline has no notch at its middle, where the middle row runs; pin 1 is at the lower left, the corner the narrow outline's notch marks and where every DIP on this board has its pin 1 (task 0's marks).

U1's 300 mil footprint: the middle row and the lower row, inside the solid outline whose notch is at its left end. Kept as an alternate, sharing the lower row with U1. Pin 1 by hand: the notch at the outline's left end runs beside the middle row's first hole, which is not found, so the grouping cannot see enough of it; pin 1 is the lower row's left end, as for U1.

The print reads 'U4' and 'SRAM(VRAM)' below the footprint's lower row. Three rows of 12 holes, as at U1: the 600 mil footprint is the upper and the lower row (the plan's Facts: U4, the 6116, a DIP-24 at 600 mil), the dashed outline above the solid one; pin 1 at the lower left, as at U1.
U4's 300 mil footprint: the middle row and the lower row, inside the solid outline whose notch is at its left end. Kept as an alternate, sharing the lower row with U4.
The edge fingers. The print reads '1' above the left end finger and '36' above the right end finger, so pin 1 is the component side's left end finger.

The expansion connector: two rows of 24 on 2.54 mm, about 6.3 mm apart, which no DIP spacing fits. The rows' end pins are task 0's scale marks. The print reads '48' at the upper row's left end, '25' at its right, '1' and '24' below the lower row's left and right ends, and 'P2' below it, so pin 1 is the lower row's left end and pins 25 to 48 run back along the upper row. The grouping found only parts of the upper row (holes there are not all found on either face).

The RF modulator: five large rings 4 mm apart below the print's 'MOD RF' strip, which reads '5' above the right end, so pin 1 is the left. The modulator's can is held by tabs in slots, which are not round holes and are not grouped here. Re-marked on 5 October 2026 after review: the first marks, (1972, 1245) and (2160, 1245) read off a crop enlarged twice, sat on the rings' lower edges, about 1.1 mm low. Each ring was read again on its own crop enlarged eight times, its outer edge's left, right, top and bottom: centres (1973, 1232), (2020, 1232.5), (2067.5, 1232.5), (2113, 1232) and (2161, 1232), 4.0 mm apart.

A controller header: seven holes 2.0 mm apart in an outline, the print reading '7' at the left end and 'P4' with '1' at the right (P41 at the half-size view), so pin 1 is the right end. Its pitch is not 2.54 mm, which the grouping's rows on 2.0 mm found, unnamed.
The other controller header: seven holes 2.0 mm apart down the board, the print reading 'P5' and '7' at the top, so pin 1 is the bottom end (read on a second crop below the first).

Power and reset: five large rings down the right edge, four 5 mm apart and the bottom one 7.5 mm further, so grouped pin by pin. The print reads '5' beside the top ring, so pin 1 is the bottom. Re-read on 5 October 2026 after review, each ring on its own crop enlarged ten times with a 2 px grid, as the middle of its hole between its edges: pin 1 had been marked about 0.5 mm high and pins 2 and 3 about 0.2 mm high.

The crystal: the print reads 'X1' and 'X'tal' beside an outline lying on the board; its two leads are the two holes at the outline's left (upper first), and the two holes at its right corners hold the can down. No pin numbers are printed; the order is the leads, upper first, then the can's two, upper first. The can's two holes re-read on 5 October 2026 after review, each on a crop enlarged twelve times with a 2 px grid: they had been marked about 0.3 mm off their middles. The leads were looked at again at eight times and kept.

The 4 MHz resonator: three holes 2.5 mm apart down the board in an outline, the print reading '3', 'X2' and '1' beside it from the top, so pin 1 is the bottom. Looked at again on 5 October 2026 after review at eight times: each pin's mark is within about 0.2 mm of its hole's middle; kept.

hidden.what: On I1-front: what hides the board and is not its printed legend, as a box (left, top, right, bottom, in the original's pixels), read by eye off its crop. board_trace.py (task 4) leaves the board under it neither copper nor print, and records its area.

marks.reason: A cream paper sticker printed "NTSC" in black, stuck over the board left of the edge fingers, below "SRAM(WRAM)". It is as light as the white print (L 0.742 against the print's 0.737), so it is marked, not told apart by colour. Its edges run from x 506 to 750 and y 1233 to 1312, a little turned; the box takes 2 pixels more each way.

parts.what: Task 5, read by eye on 5 October 2026. I4 and I5 (Evan-Amos's NES-CPU-07, top and solder side) and I3 (the PAL NES-CPU-11): points in the original's pixels, (0, 0) the centre of the top left pixel, each read off a crop enlarged as `crop` says with a grid labelled in the original's pixels in strips outside the crop. Passives: board millimetres, each lead a hole read off I1-front rectified at 16 px/mm with a 1 mm grid and the scan's holes numbered on it, and the part looked at on I4 with those holes drawn through I4's fit; board_parts.py moves each lead to the scan's pad within 0.6 mm of it and records which it did.

seeds.what: U6's corner pins where the lead meets its pad, to start the fit only (crop 60 px square enlarged 4 times, 5 px grid)

midlines.what: U7 and U8, the MN74HC368s, whose leads show grey between two highlights, not as light flats: the midline at the first and last lead columns, x the middle of the two leads (top and bottom), y half way between the body's two long edges, read on crops 90 by 200 px enlarged 4 times with a 10 px grid

parts.reason: body edges y 412.5 and 534.5 at the left column, 413 and 536 at the right; leads x 2567 to 2569 and 2918 to 2919
body edges y 668 and 792 at the left column, 668 and 793 at the right; leads x 2566 to 2567 and 2917

outlines.what: Each body's outline as seen from above, [left, top, right, bottom] in pixels: its top, which stands above the board and leans away from the middle of the picture (not corrected; about its height times its distance from the middle over the camera's height, about 0.8 m). Read on crops enlarged 1 to 2 times with a 10 to 50 px grid

boxes.reason: the black body between its ears (the ears, x 247 to 520 and 2800 to 3062, y 2405 to 2665, hang below the board's edge and are not in the box); its top edge at y 2213 is where it meets the tinned edge fingers
the metal frame round the socket, left side x 898 to 902, right 2360 to 2364, top 600 to 605, bottom 876 to 881
the cream housing, open towards the board's top edge; seven pins
the cream housing, open towards the board's right edge
the blue switch block for POWER and RESET, which runs past the board's right edge
the blue crystal lying flat, a wire strap over it
the RF modulator's frame, lid off: its left wall x 3175 to 3180, right 4435 to 4445, top 1955 to 1965, bottom 3150 to 3160; its jacks and bracket stand outside the box

seeds.what: U6's corner pins' solder joints (the solder side, mirrored), to start the fit only

looked.what: Where the joint finder found fewer joints than holes: each connector's and crystal's holes drawn on I5 through its fit, on a crop enlarged once or twice with a 20 px grid, and what the crop showed; `sits` is what was judged from it

P1.what: no holes: the edge fingers, which the connector clamps; on I4 its body lies across them, its outline's middle 0.9 mm right of the fingers' middle and its ends past both end fingers (parts.json "beside")

P3.what: every hole has its joint under the cross (pins 1 to 5)

P4.what: every hole has its joint under the cross (7)

P5.what: every hole has its joint under the cross (7)

P6.what: every hole has its joint under the cross (5 large joints)

X1.what: every hole has its joint under the cross (the two leads and the two strap holes)

X2.what: every hole has its joint, pin 1 about 0.5 mm from the cross

P2.what: every hole has its joint under the cross; the finder missed pin 3's, whose highlight runs off its disc

outlines.what: As I4's outlines, on I3 (20 mm lens: a top leans further)

boxes.reason: the orange crystal lying flat, a wire strap over it; its lower edge meets the expansion socket's frame; so the box is what is seen, its lower part hidden
the modulator's can, lid on, "ALPS" embossed; its left wall x 3690 to 3720 and its top wall y 2290 to 2310 seen edge on

passives.what: Each two- or more-lead part fitted on I4, at the holes the CPU-10's print gives its reference: kind axial, radial or other, the part as seen, and its leads in board millimetres (pins: an array's pin count, where only its end leads are given). Not fitted on I4 though printed on the CPU-10, and not drawn: R14, R15, R16, R17, C6, C7. C2: the CPU-07 has an axial part on holes about 8.7 mm apart where the CPU-10 has C2's two holes 5.2 mm apart; not drawn

caseFeatures.what: Task 8. Lines are segments marked by hand along an edge (two points, an optional half width of the search in px), each fitted by case_measure.py as spike.py fits its lines; points and boxes are read by eye. The patent's features (O1) are boxes [left, top, right, bottom] or circles [x, y, r] in the page's pixels, read off crops enlarged 0.8 to 1.6 times with a 10 to 40 px grid, to about 1 px (0.2 to 0.3 mm). Photographs' features are polygons or points in the original's pixels, read off crops enlarged 0.6 to 1.2 times with a 25 to 100 px grid, to about 3 px; each is said where it is used to be in its face's plane or not.

FIG 3.what: The front. The door's two sides and its lower edge; its tab; the black band, the top shell's part and the controller block below the seam; the two ports' frames; the recessed panel round the buttons, the LED and POWER's and RESET's middle outlines; the feet below the body.

FIG 4.what: The rear, seen from behind: its left is the case's right. The recessed window, open at the base, with the power jack, the channel switch and the RF jack (each its outline and, for the round ones, its centre), and the label strip; the notch in the base; the black band.

FIG 5.what: The top, its front at the bottom of the page. The door's outline on the top, from its rear edge to the front; the black band; the ribbed vents between its two black ends (each rib drawn as a bar of two lines; case_measure.py counts the lines across the band between the two x in ribsCount); POWER and RESET seen from above, standing out past the front.

FIG 6.what: The underside, the case turned over about its left to right axis: its front at the top of the page and the case's right on the page's right, as its features show (the controller ports' bracket at the top right, the rear window's bump at the bottom right, the AV jacks' bump on the right edge nearer the bottom). The four feet, the screw holes, the expansion cover and its inner panel, the two straps of the moulding, the vents, the other moulded panels.

FIG 7.what: The side with the AV jacks, its rear on the right of the page (the jacks and the oval recess are nearer the rear, as O2-FL shows them): the jacks' window, the two jacks' centres (video nearer the rear, audio in front of it, as I7-FL and O2-FL show their colours), the oval, the moulded tab at the base.

O2-FL.what: The front face, rectified on its four bounding lines: the top's near long edge, the top shell's two ends (task 0's marks) and the base, where the bottom shell meets the table. Lines: the seam either side of the black block, the bottom shell's two ends leaning in (on the left end its silhouette; on the right end, which the camera sees, the change of light where the end turns away), the door's sides and its lower edge, the panel's three edges, the black block's right edge. The smaller features are boxes read off the rectified front (onFace). The top face, rectified on task 0's four corners: the door's rear edge on the top, the black band's two sides (the right one along its rear black end, where the vents' ends do not cross it) and the ends of the ribbed vents.

onFace.what: Boxes [u0, z0, u1, z1] in millimetres on the front face, u from its left end and z up from the base, read by eye off the rectified front that case_measure.py draws (out/case-front-left.png and -right.png, 8 px/mm, a 5 mm grid), to about 0.3 mm. The buttons stand about 1 mm out of the face (FIG 5), so their holes in the panel, which lie in it, are read: each hole's two sides and its top, its bottom hidden under the button's face and put 14 mm below its top, where the button's front face's bottom reads (13.9 to 14.0).

O2-BR.what: The rear face, seen from behind, rectified on its bounding lines: the top's near long edge, the top shell's two ends (task 0's marks) and the base right of the notch. Lines: the bottom shell's two ends leaning in (the profile's held-out check), the window panel's base, the top's far short edge (a line square to the face), the notch's two sides. The window's panel is set back from the face: a point on it reads off its place through the face's homography along the far short edge's direction, by as much as the panel's base reads above the base, and case_measure.py takes that off. The features are boxes read off the rectified rear (onFace).

onFace.what: Boxes [u0, z0, u1, z1] in millimetres on the rear face seen from behind, u from its left end as seen (the case's right) and z up from the base, read by eye off the rectified rear (out/case-rear.png, 8 px/mm, a 5 mm grid). The window's outline lies in the face; everything inside it is on the panel set back from the face, read as it shows, and case_measure.py takes the panel's shift off.

I7-FL.what: The modulator's rear face on the NTSC board (I7-FL, the board component side up, looked at from beyond its edge fingers), by its four corners, its width the modulator's from parts.json (its x extent on I4). Only places along the face are used, so its height need not be known. The jacks: the RF jack's body where it meets the face (its ring stands out of it), the channel switch's slot, the power jack's socket.

HOF06601.what: The PAL set's photograph of the bottom shell from above with the board in it, solder side up, the case's front at the top: the rim's four outer edges (the left one is the case's right), and two of the board's mounting holes as a seed; case_measure.py then finds the board's holes and the ICs' end pins near where the seed puts them.

O4.what: The PAL top shell's front band straight on (task 0's corners): the words, polygons by eye.

O5.what: The PAL underside, seen from below and turned so that the case's rear is at the top of the picture and its right on the left (the AV jacks' bump on the left edge, the controller bracket at the bottom left), taken close with a 19 mm lens, so its outline (at the seam, about 45 mm further off than the bottom) is not in the bottom's plane. The bottom is rectified instead on its six screw holes, which lie in it, against their places on the patent's FIG 6; each hole is a seed marked by eye and found as the dark blob near it. The two labels and the expansion cover are polygons by eye; the feet are circles by eye [x, y, r].
